correctness.rationale: For any acute triangle the \(n=4\) cyclic line word must repeat exactly one of the three lines in opposite positions; a two-line alternation has only the common vertex as affine-return fixed point, but the map sends a vertex to the opposite line. The four unique affine return candidates have the exact strict branch inequalities in RESULT.md. On the isosceles base they reduce to \(4s^2-2s-1<0\), while on either leg the necessary condition reduces to \((s^2-1/2)^2<0\), an impossibility. At equality the two leg points are fixed-on-tie, so the cutoff is open. Period-three has exactly two possible cyclic orientations; the explicit representative passes its strict tests iff \(s<(1+\sqrt3)/2\). All three cycles have strict return contraction, with the signed period-three multiplier negative and period-four multiplier positive. The standalone exact-rational verifier exhaustively enumerated all length-three and length-four line-word candidates at twelve rational heights and agreed with the analytical classification. This finite test is a check, not the proof.
